title: A flat affine chart covering relative associated primes gives a universally injective section map
statement: Let $R\to C\to D$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings and let $P$ be a $C$-module. Suppose $C$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $P$ is a finitely presented $C$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], $P$ is flat over $R$, and $D$ is flat over $C$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose the image of $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains every prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ which is an element-annihilator associated prime of the $C$-module $P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, where $\mathfrak p\subset R$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes, def-weil-residue-field]. Then the canonical $R$-linear map $u:P\to P\otimes_CD$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, is universally injective over $R$: for every $R$-module $L$, the map $u\otimes_R1_L:P\otimes_RL\to(P\otimes_CD)\otimes_RL$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No faithful-flatness assumption on $C\to D$ is made.

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C$ with inverse image $\mathfrak p$ in $R$, let $u_{\mathfrak q}:P_{\mathfrak q}\to(P\otimes_CD)_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization of $u$ at $C\setminus\mathfrak q$. The universal-injectivity localization criterion [lem-trf-universal-injective-check-stalks], applied to $R\to C$ and the $C$-linear map $u$, says that $u$ is universally injective over $R$ if and only if every $u_{\mathfrak q}$ is universally injective over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. That node tests with $L\otimes_Ru$; the flip isomorphisms $x\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes x$ given by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] conjugate $L\otimes_Ru$ to $u\otimes_R1_L$ (check on pure tensors), so the two tests agree, over $R$ and over each $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus it suffices to prove that every $u_{\mathfrak q}$ is universally injective over $R_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 05DH proof, first sentence, invoking Algebra Tag 05CL (lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks).

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$; we check hypotheses (local map, essential finite presentation, finite presentation, flatness) of [lem-sfb-assassin-cover-universal-section-injection-local] for $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ and $N=P_{\mathfrak q}$, where $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is $D$ localized at the image of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. (a) Elements of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ map into $C\setminus\mathfrak q$, so $r/a\mapsto r/a$ is a ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}$; it sends $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ into $\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q}$, so it is local. (b) A presentation $C\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] gives the finitely presented $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $B=R_{\mathfrak p}[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$, which is $C$ localized at the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$; $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of $B$ at the image $W$ of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$, by $(c/a)/(c'/a')\mapsto ca'/(ac')$ with inverse $c/s\mapsto(c/1)/(s/1)$. So $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}$ is essentially of finite presentation. (c) A presentation $C^b\to C^a\to P\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] localizes, by exactness of localization, to $C_{\mathfrak q}^b\to C_{\mathfrak q}^a\to P_{\mathfrak q}\to0$. (d) $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] (for $R\to C$, $P$ and $C\setminus\mathfrak q$); $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ acts invertibly on it, so it is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module through $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] makes it $R_{\mathfrak p}$-flat. (e) $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is $C$-flat by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] (for $C\to D$, the module $D$ and the image of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$), and the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] for $C\to C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ makes $C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ flat. (f) The map $P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{C_{\mathfrak q}}D_{\mathfrak q}\to(P\otimes_CD)_{\mathfrak q}$, $(x/s)\otimes(d/t)\mapsto(x\otimes d)/(st)$, is an isomorphism (inverse $(x\otimes d)/s\mapsto(x/s)\otimes(d/1)$) under which $x/s\mapsto(x/s)\otimes1$ becomes $u_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 05DH proof, second paragraph: apply Lemma 05DG (lemma-base-change-universally-flat-local) to R_p→S_q→S'_q and N_q.

proof.text: Image hypothesis. Put $F=C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $M=P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; $C$ acts on $M$ through $C\to F$. The maps $[x/s]\mapsto(x\otimes1)/s$ and $(x\otimes(r/a))/s\mapsto[rx/(as)]$ are inverse $C_{\mathfrak q}$-isomorphisms $P_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak q}$ ($\mathfrak pP$ maps to $0$, $a\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ acts invertibly). Let $Q\subset C_{\mathfrak q}$ be a prime with inverse image $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ in $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $Q=\operatorname{Ann}_{C_{\mathfrak q}}(w)$, $w=z/s$, $z\in M$, $s\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$; let $\mathfrak q''\subseteq\mathfrak q$ be its inverse image in $C$, so $\mathfrak q''\cap R=\mathfrak p$. The field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its ideals are $0$ and itself), and $F$ is of finite type over it (images of generators of $C$), so $F$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and $\mathfrak q''F=(a_1\otimes1,\dots,a_n\otimes1)$ for some $a_i\in\mathfrak q''$. Since $(a_i/1)w=0$, the kernel criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $t_i\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $t_ia_iz=0$; put $t=t_1\cdots t_n\notin\mathfrak q$ and $z'=tz$. If $a\in\mathfrak q''$, write $a\otimes1=\sum\varphi_i(a_i\otimes1)$ in $F$; then $az'=\sum\varphi_i\,t\,a_iz=0$. If $az'=0$, then $(t/1)(a/1)w=0$ with $t/1$ a unit, so $a/1\in Q$ and $a\in\mathfrak q''$. Hence $\mathfrak q''=\operatorname{Ann}_C(z')$ is an associated prime of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes] with inverse image $\mathfrak p$, so the hypothesis gives a prime $\mathfrak r\subset D$ over $\mathfrak q''$. As $\mathfrak q''\subseteq\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak r$ misses the image of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] it is the inverse image of a prime $\mathfrak r'$ of $D_{\mathfrak q}$. The inverse image of $\mathfrak r'$ in $C_{\mathfrak q}$ and $Q$ both contract to $\mathfrak q''$ in $C$, so they are equal by injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding]. Thus $Q$ lies in the image of $\operatorname{Spec}D_{\mathfrak q}\to\operatorname{Spec}C_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 05DH proof, second sentence ('Thus we may apply Lemma 05DG'), hypothesis (6) of Tag 05DG for R_p -> S_q -> S'_q; the transfer of associated primes follows Algebra Tag 0310 (lemma-associated-primes-localize), part (2), over the Noetherian fibre ring.

proof.text: By Steps 2 and 3 all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-assassin-cover-universal-section-injection-local] hold for $R_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}\to D_{\mathfrak q}$ and $P_{\mathfrak q}$, so $P_{\mathfrak q}\to P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{C_{\mathfrak q}}D_{\mathfrak q}$, which is $u_{\mathfrak q}$ by Step 2(f), is universally injective over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Since $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, Step 1 proves that $u$ is universally injective over $R$.
